Goodbye Niketu Iralu: Peace icon who emerged from cradle of Naga armed rebellion

Nagaland today bid adieu to iconic peace activist Niketu Iralu who died this week. For over six decades, Iralu had been offering a healing touch to the fractured Naga society. He was born in Khonoma, the same village where Angami Zapu Phizo, father of Naga insurgency, was born. Iralu was related to Phizo but took a very different path.

Dead Rat Found In Branded Namkeen Packet In Kanpur Dehat; Food Safety Department Issues Notice

A serious food safety concern has emerged from Kanpur Dehat after a dead rat was reportedly discovered inside a sealed packet of Bikanervala Navratna mixture namkeen. The packet, purchased at a grocery store on Mughal Road, prompted immediate outrage and demands for a strict investigation regarding hygiene standards. Following a formal complaint and viral video of the incident, the Food and Safety Department in Uttar Pradesh issued a notice to the manufacturer. Officials sent a regional food safety inspection team to conduct an on-spot investigation, record witness statements, and question company representatives to enforce compliance with food safety laws.

RTO Begins Marathi Proficiency Test For Auto Drivers In Thane; Non-Compliant Drivers Served Notices

The Regional Transport Office in Thane, Maharashtra, has initiated checks on auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers to assess their working knowledge of the Marathi language. Under the Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules, Marathi proficiency is compulsory for obtaining commercial driving licenses and badges. During the drive, officials test drivers on basic Marathi skills. Drivers unable to speak or understand the language are being issued notices requiring them to acquire working knowledge within one month. The mandate has sparked debate among transport unions, who previously protested against verifying existing license holders, citing concerns over language politics.

Furthermore, criticisms were raised against the central governing model, citing the monopolization of business and resources that hinders self-reliance. Rizwan Arshad Terms Delimitation 'Unfair', Warns South May Become 'Tax Slaves' At Southern CMs Meet

A special regional report highlights major political, economic, and civic developments across Southern Indian states. At the Southern Chief Ministers' meeting chaired by the Union Home Minister in Mahabalipuram, Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad criticized the proposed delimitation exercise. Arshad endorsed Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar's resolution to freeze Lok Sabha seats at 543 based on the 1971 census, raising concerns over reduced tax devolution despite Southern states contributing 33 percent to India's GDP. Representatives from Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh addressed critical state priorities, including inter-state water disputes over the Cauvery and Mekedatu rivers, NEET, and federal fund allocation. In Tamil Nadu, the state government clarified an administrative error regarding student protest circulars. Meanwhile, in Bengaluru, an engineer created an artificial intelligence app to report potholes to civic authorities. In Andhra Pradesh, political controversy emerged over alleged examination irregularities under the previous YSRCP regime, while Telangana's Nalgonda police arrested two juveniles in connection with a local murder investigation.

31st Southern Zonal Council Meets: Focus On Bullet Train Corridor, Water Issues And Women's Quota

The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting brought together Chief Ministers and representatives from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar, and Lakshadweep to address critical interstate and centre-state matters. Key discussions revolved around enhancing regional cooperation, developing transport infrastructure, and resolving longstanding interstate disputes. Proposals were introduced for a bullet train corridor connecting Amaravati, Bengaluru, and Chennai, alongside the interlinking of the Godavari and Cauvery rivers to mitigate ongoing water sharing conflicts. The council also deliberated on the Mullaperiyar dam construction, regional port development under Mission Samudra, and the annulment of the Mineral Act Amendment. Additionally, concerns were raised regarding parliamentary delimitation, with calls to implement a one-third reservation for women within the existing parliamentary strength. Interstate water management, particularly concerning the Cauvery and Mullaperiyar dams, remained a central focus as participating states sought long-term cooperative solutions to balance drinking water, agricultural, and industrial needs across the southern region.

Amit Shah Chairs South Zonal Meet: Delimitation, Water Sharing & Rail Links Take Centre Stage

First images have emerged from the Southern Zonal Council meeting chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah alongside key southern chief ministers and union territory representatives. Discussions focused on crucial interstate concerns including delimitation, water sharing, trade, and transport connectivity. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu highlighted the need for improved rail infrastructure and bullet train links between southern capital cities. Meanwhile, state leaders raised strong concerns over delimitation, emphasizing that southern states must not lose parliamentary representation. Issues surrounding fiscal federalism, Cauvery water distribution, and interstate coordination against drug abuse were also addressed during the meeting.

Additionally, the Chief Minister raises the issue of delimitation, stating that public policy must not penalize southern states for fulfilling national objectives or diminish their political representation. The discussion also covers broader inter-state matters affecting southern states.

Congress Attacks PM Modi, BJP Counters CWC Label, Flashpoints On NEET And Vande Mataram Escalate

A political war of words has erupted between the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party following the Congress Working Committee meeting. The Congress mounted a direct attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that his political standing has weakened due to key national issues such as the COVID-19 pandemic response, NEET examination irregularities, and paper leaks. Party leaders emphasized that the opposition has continuously questioned the government on matters including alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement and the Vande Mataram singing row. In response, the Bharatiya Janata Party countered by calling the CWC the Congress Whitewash Committee, accusing the opposition of refusing to acknowledge its own political mistakes. Congress spokesperson Abhishek Dubey further asserted that criticisms from various public figures reflect dissatisfaction with government policies. Both parties continue to clash over parliamentary functioning, policy decisions, and national priorities.

Mekedatu Row: Karnataka Pitches Cauvery Water Cooperation To Union Minister Amit Shah

In a meeting with Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Karnataka representative DK Shivakumar raised the long-standing Cauvery water issue, advocating a shift from water sharing to water cooperation based on equity, transparency, and mutual respect while protecting Karnataka's lawful share. Shivakumar emphasized that the proposed Mekedatu project would benefit farmers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry alongside Karnataka. Reporter Apoorva noted that the proposal comes amid rising tensions between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, where the state government remains firm on constructing the Mekedatu dam for drinking water needs despite ongoing opposition from Tamil Nadu and proceedings before the Supreme Court and Cauvery tribunal.

Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar Dies At 80 While Serving Life Sentence In Tihar Jail

Former Congress Member of Parliament and leader Sajjan Kumar has passed away at the age of 80 while serving life imprisonment in Tihar Jail. Hospital sources from Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital confirmed that he was declared brought dead after being brought unconscious from jail. Kumar was serving multiple life sentences following his conviction for murder, rioting, and arson in cases arising out of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. He had previously filed court petitions seeking bail due to severe health conditions, but medical committees advised that hospitalization was unnecessary. A former three-time Lok Sabha MP from Outer Delhi who resigned from the party after his conviction, he was also facing additional ongoing trials.
